title: Annotatio VI §.VI reply: sacraments restricted extrinsically to God’s requisite, not arbitrium
pass_a_gloss: Reply (a) Indirectly: The same can be said by reason of spiritual Eating. (b) Directly: Sacraments are restricted and suspended not Intrinsically and Constitutively, but Extrinsically, Effectively and Objectively. They are restricted to requisites of man, but such as are God’s work, not men’s. Hence the consequence is denied: Sacraments do not operate unless man’s faith is supposed, Therefore the Sacraments’ Operation depends on Man’s arbitrium and work. Just as it does not hold, even on Lutheran terms: The Word of GOD works Conversion; Or: God or the Holy Spirit converts man and gifts him with faith unless he reject GOD’s grace, Therefore man’s Conversion depends on human arbitrium — for because that very power of receiving and not receiving, in the composed sense, is GOD’s work, not man’s, namely gifted by preventing grace with the announcing of the divine word, Conversion is indeed restricted to a Requisite in man, but to such as not man but GOD’s virtue and power work, so that it proceeds not from man but from GOD. In this way all that the most distinguished Man brought, both from himself and from Luther, also beat the air.
pass_b_english: Reply: the same could be said of spiritual eating. Sacraments are restricted not constitutively but extrinsically — to requisites that are God’s work, not man’s arbitrium.

“No faith, no operation ⇒ depends on human will” fails the same way Lutheran conversion talk fails: the power to receive or not is itself God’s preventing gift with the word. So the Wittenberg/Luther citations beat the air.
source_text: Resp. (a) Indirectè: Idem dici posse ratione spiritualis Manducationis. (b) Directè: Sacramenta esse restricta & suspensa non Intrinsecè & Constitutivè, sed Extrinsecè, Effectivè & Objectivè. Esse restricta ad requisita hominis, sed talia, quæ opus Dei, non hominum sunt. Hinc negatur consequentia: Sacramenta non operantur, nisi suppositâ fide hominis, Ergo Sacramentorum Operatio dependet ab Hominis arbitrio & opere. Quemadmodum non valet, vel juxta Lutheranos: Verbum DEI operatur Conversionem; Vel: Deus seu Spiritus S. convertit hominem eúmque donat fide, nisi rejiciat gratiam DEI, Ergo Conversio hominis dependet ab humano arbitrio: Nam quia illa ipsa potentia recipiendi & non recipiendi, in sensu composito, est opus DEI, non hominis, utpote, per gratiam prævenientem, cum annunciatione verbi divini, donata, Conversio quidem restringitur ad Requisitum in homine, sed ad tale, quod non homo, sed virtus & potentia DEI, operantur, ut non ab homine, sed DEO proficiscatur. Hoc pacto aërem quoque feriunt omnia, à Clariss. Viro, tam ex se, quam ex Luthero allata.
